The Tatsu's performance envelope is built around a Shinobi 210 XL engine, a weight-saving choice that liberates an impressive forty-one tons of pod space for mission-specific equipment. Wakazashi engineers deliberately chose Naketsu MetalWeave standard armor over the lighter ferro-aluminum alternative to avoid restricting that pod capacity, and the resulting sixteen and a half tons of protection is exceptional for a craft of this mass. Structural integrity of seven gives the Tatsu solid resistance to the stresses of atmospheric combat, while the airframe itself owes part of its aerodynamic profile and maneuverability to careful study of the Dragon Dove, a native avian species found on Dover.

The base chassis mounts only ten double heat sinks, a deliberate trade-off that places the heat management burden on the pod configuration rather than the fixed structure. This approach means pilots must understand the thermal demands of their chosen loadout before entering combat, as the Tatsu provides limited safety margin against overheating without config-level supplemental heat sinks. Configuration designers have accounted for this constraint, and most loadouts include additional heat sinks as part of their pod allocation. The Garret T22 communications suite and Neko Megane 6 targeting system provide capable situational awareness and fire control across the aircraft's diverse weapons fits.

The Tatsu stands as the Draconis Combine's first OmniFighter designed and built from the ground up. Developed by Wakazashi Enterprises at their Chatham production facility, the design emerged from the Combine's determination to field a true purpose-built OmniFighter after the limitations of their earlier Sai Omni conversion became apparent. Entering mass production in 3063, the Tatsu was conceived with a singular focus: delivering maximum damage to ground-based targets. The design philosophy sacrificed some defensive efficiency in armor type to maximize available pod space, granting commanders an unusual degree of flexibility in configuring the aircraft for diverse missions. The result is a capable ground-attack platform that has earned a place in the hangar bays of some of the Draconis Combine's most prestigious aerospace regiments.

Fielded during the Dark Age, the F configuration reflects updated technology priorities by mounting large re-engineered lasers in each wing and in the nose, supplemented by an MML-7 launcher in each wing. The re-engineered large lasers reduce heat output compared to standard large lasers while maintaining comparable range and damage output, and the MML-7 launchers provide ammunition-based strike capability that complements the energy weapon loadout. This configuration stands as a more balanced approach than the Jihad-era variants, blending reliable energy weapons with moderate missile capability for versatile multi-role operations in the resource-constrained Dark Age environment. BV (2.0): 1,515.

Following the Draconis Combine's successful reverse-engineering of OmniMech technology in 3052, Wakazashi Enterprises turned their attention to the greater engineering challenge of developing a compatible OmniFighter. The complexity of aerospace fighter design proved far more demanding than BattleMech conversion work, and early development stalled as Wakazashi engineers struggled to adapt OmniPod technology to aerodynamic airframes. As a stopgap, Wakazashi produced a limited Omni conversion of their existing Sai light fighter in the late 3050s. That design, while a welcome morale boost for the DCMS, was widely regarded as a flawed compromise rather than a genuine solution.

Wakazashi engineering teams were already developing a clean-sheet replacement before the Sai conversion had reached regiment strength. Work on the new design proceeded through the early 3060s, drawing lessons from both the Sai conversion's shortcomings and Clan OmniFighter performance observed during the Invasion. The prototype flew for the first time in 3062 and passed its trials with sufficient results for the Coordinator to authorize full production. Mass production at the Chatham facility began in 3063, making the Tatsu the first Inner Sphere OmniFighter the Combine had fielded that owed nothing to an existing standard fighter design.

Adoption followed the pattern typical of high-priority Combine equipment. The Sword of the Light, Ryuken, and Genyosha regiments incorporated the Tatsu quickly, drawn by the low maintenance burden that OmniPod technology shared with their existing OmniMech fleets. Pilots in these elite formations valued the ability to reconfigure aircraft between missions without extensive supply complications. As production output at Chatham grew, the Tatsu gradually filtered into DCMS Regular regiments, with confirmed sightings eventually extending to second-line formations such as the Seventh Ghost Regiment.

Wakazashi's modifications were extensive. The Graceful Crane's structure was heavily reinforced with an armored chassis, allowing it to mount the maximum possible armor protection for its airframe. Three tons of military-grade communications equipment enabled the Warlord to maintain contact with all subordinate commands even in flight, effectively transforming the aircraft into an airborne headquarters. In extremis, the communications suite could project an ECCM field to counter hostile electronic warfare.

Ejection seats were provided for all passengers and crew as a safety measure, and the cargo bay was expanded to hold armored limousines for secure ground transit upon landing. The Tsuru's most distinctive feature was its wing-mounted and aft-quarter chaff pods--four in total. Though chaff dispensing technology had existed since the earliest days of powered flight, it had become a rarity by the thirty-first century due to advances in missile guidance systems. Wakazashi included them as part of a no-expense-spared approach, and the STOL capability ensured the craft could operate from shorter airstrips.

The Tsuru was born from the ambitions of Warlord Vasily Cherenkoff of the Dieron Military District, who shortly after his promotion in 3021 commissioned Wakazashi Enterprises to create a military transport befitting his rank. The brief demanded a swift aircraft capable of carrying the Warlord and his senior staff in safety and luxury, yet equipped with military-grade communications for command duties in flight. Rather than design from scratch, Wakazashi elected to modify their existing Graceful Crane luxury airliner--itself a successful imitation of Avanti Industries' Zanadu Air Bus that had debuted in 3007. The resulting one-hundred-ton fixed-wing support craft was designated the Tsuru, adopting the traditional Japanese word for crane.

The Tsuru served as Warlord Cherenkoff's personal transport within the Dieron Military District, where it provided both mobile command capability and the visible prestige expected of a senior Combine military leader. The Graceful Crane's lavish interior fittings were retained and enhanced with purpose-built luxury quarters, while first-class accommodations served the Warlord's senior staff during extended flights between district commands.

The Tsuru's lineage traced back to Avanti Industries' Zanadu Air Bus, which debuted in 3004 and quickly became synonymous with luxury air travel across the Inner Sphere. When the Zanadu spawned a wave of imitators from rival states, Wakazashi Enterprises' Graceful Crane appeared in 3007 as the Combine's answer, becoming an indispensable status symbol for corporate executives throughout the Draconis Combine. The Tsuru represented the militarization of that successful civilian luxury platform.

Pleased with the resulting design, Warlord Cherenkoff requested only one final personal touch: he ordered his Tsuru painted red, to match the color scheme of his personal Atlas BattleMek. The aircraft became a highly recognizable symbol of the Warlord's authority throughout the Dieron District, combining the prestige expected of a luxury VIP transport with the practical command and communications capabilities demanded by a senior military officer responsible for coordinating forces across multiple planetary garrisons within one of the Combine's most strategically vital military districts.
